content: Provider-selection UX in shipping desktop tools: Zed (Settings > AI > LLM Providers) and Obsidian Copilot (Settings > Copilot > BYOK) both store keys in the OS keychain, never in the app's settings/config JSON, and both allow an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible base URL plus a free-text model name. Neither documents an explicit key-validation step at entry time — validation happens on first real request, which is a known UX complaint (zed-industries/zed#26106: 'No LLM provider selected' after adding a key). A visible Test/Verify affordance is the gap those products leave open.
